title: Futur proche
goal: By the end of this lesson you can talk about plans and the near future with aller + infinitive, make it negative, ask questions with it, and recognise the Quebec spoken forms j'vas and m'as.

body: The futur proche works exactly like English 'going to': conjugate *aller* in the present, then add a verb in the infinitive. *Je vais manger.* = I'm going to eat.
Only *aller* changes; the second verb never moves from its infinitive form: *nous allons partir*, *elles vont travailler*.

head: Pronoun
aller
+ infinitive
English
rows: he / she / we are going to go out

learn.tip: Two verbs, one conjugated: vais + infinitive.

learn.h: Time words that go with it
body: The futur proche usually comes with a time word: *ce soir* (tonight), *demain* (tomorrow), *ce week-end* or *en fin de semaine* (this weekend), *la semaine prochaine* (next week), *l'année prochaine* (next year), *bientôt* (soon), *dans deux heures* (in two hours).
The time word can start or end the sentence: *Demain, je vais travailler.* / *Je vais travailler demain.*
*Ne … pas* goes around the conjugated verb *aller*, not the infinitive: *Je ne vais pas manger.* *Il ne va pas venir.*

Questions use the patterns you know: intonation (*Tu vas venir?*), *est-ce que* (*Est-ce que tu vas venir?*) or inversion (*Vas-tu venir?* / *Va-t-il pleuvoir?*). With a question word: *Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire?* *Quand est-ce que vous allez partir?*
learn.tip: Ne … pas hugs vais, not the infinitive.

body: Yes, you can say *Je vais aller au cinéma.* (I'm going to go to the movies.) It sounds completely natural.
In daily speech, though, the present often does the job when the plan is clear: *Je vais au cinéma ce soir.*

In Quebec speech, *je vais* is very often *j'vas* (you met it in lesson 11): *J'vas aller au dep.* Even shorter, and very informal, is *m'as*: *M'as te le dire.* (I'm gonna tell you.) Understand *m'as*, but don't write it.
With the reflexive verb *se voir* (to see each other), the *e* disappears: *On va s'voir demain.* And the Quebec *-tu* question particle attaches to *aller*: *Tu vas-tu venir?*

examples.fr: Tu vas manger avec nous ce soir?
examples.en: Are you going to eat with us tonight?
It's going to rain this afternoon.
We're going to watch a movie.

examples.fr: Nous allons voyager en Gaspésie cet été.
examples.en: We're going to travel in the Gaspé this summer.
You're going to like this restaurant.
My parents are going to arrive on Sunday.

examples.fr: Je ne vais pas sortir ce soir.
examples.en: I'm not going to go out tonight.

examples.fr: Elle ne va pas aimer ça.
examples.en: She's not going to like that.

examples.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire en fin de semaine?
examples.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

examples.fr: Est-ce que vous allez prendre l'autobus?
examples.en: Are you going to take the bus?
I'm going to go to the corner store.

examples.fr: Le film va commencer dans dix minutes.
examples.en: The movie is going to start in ten minutes.
When are they going to leave?

examples.note: c'est le fun → ça va être le fun

examples.fr: On va se voir la semaine prochaine.
examples.en: We'll see each other next week.

quebec.intro: The futur proche is the everyday future in Quebec. In speech, 'je vais' becomes 'j'vas' or even 'm'as', and the '-tu' particle turns plans into quick questions.

items.en: I'm going to go to the movies.
items.note: j'vas is very common in casual speech
m'as = je vais; very informal, spoken only
the e of se drops in speech
ne dropped, as usual in speech

drills.why: Ne … pas surrounds the conjugated verb aller.
M'as is very informal Quebec speech for je vais.

drills.en: They're going to arrive at eight.

Quebec speech: mah. It means je vais.

listen.title: Les plans de la fin de semaine

dialogue.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire en fin de semaine?
dialogue.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

dialogue.fr: Samedi, j'vas aller au marché Jean-Talon avec ma blonde.
dialogue.en: On Saturday, I'm going to go to the Jean-Talon market with my girlfriend.

dialogue.fr: Dimanche, on va rester à la maison. Il va pleuvoir.
dialogue.en: On Sunday, we're going to stay home. It's going to rain.

dialogue.fr: Moi, je vais regarder la game de hockey. Tu vas-tu venir?
dialogue.en: Me, I'm going to watch the hockey game. Are you going to come?

dialogue.fr: Oui, bonne idée! La game va commencer à quelle heure?
dialogue.en: Yes, good idea! What time is the game going to start?

dialogue.fr: À sept heures. On va manger de la pizza.
dialogue.en: At seven. We're going to eat pizza.

questions.q: Where is B going on Saturday?
Why is B staying home on Sunday?
What time does the game start?

speak.prompt: Say three things you are going to do this weekend.
speak.model: Samedi, je vais faire l'épicerie. Dimanche, je vais aller au parc et je vais regarder un film.

speak.prompt: Say two things you are NOT going to do tomorrow.
speak.model: Demain, je ne vais pas travailler et je ne vais pas faire le ménage.

speak.prompt: Invite a friend to come watch a movie, first in standard French, then the casual Quebec way.
speak.model: Est-ce que tu vas venir regarder un film ce soir? / Tu vas-tu venir écouter un film à soir?

write.prompt: Write 5–6 sentences about your plans for next week, using at least three different time words.
write.model: La semaine prochaine, je vais être très occupé. Lundi, je vais travailler en ville. Mardi soir, je vais aller au cours de français. Mercredi, mes parents vont arriver de Toronto. On va manger au restaurant. En fin de semaine, nous allons visiter Québec.

quiz.q: The futur proche is formed with…
Which verb is conjugated in 'Elle va chanter'?
quiz.why: Only aller is conjugated; chanter stays in the infinitive.
Invert tu and vas: Vas-tu venir?
Dans + time = in that much time from now.

quiz.q: Is 'Je vais aller au parc' correct?
quiz.why: Aller + aller is perfectly normal French.

options: casual Quebec speech for je vais manger
quiz.why: J'vas is the everyday Quebec spoken form of je vais.
-tu after the verb marks a yes/no question in Quebec speech.
On takes the il/elle form: on va.
